note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason:
Pull request #3100 (cinatra#3080, fix leg 7) carries this record. The review target's props builder passed an absent content projection unconditionally and said so in its own comment — the versioned server content channel (enabler 0.3 of the lifecycle plan, cinatra#3027) was never called for a review target at all — so every markdown target on every review surface drew the display's content-absent floor whatever was in it. The eighth proof round measured that on a real run: a produced text/markdown post, pinned by the gate, drew "No markdown is available to show for the revision being viewed" over a document sitting readable in the store. Wiring the channel is what fixes it.

WHAT THE RAISE IS, as a module set: exactly THREE first-party modules enter each of these four routes' graphs through src/app/artifacts/[id]/review-target-prepare.ts, which every one of them already reaches — src/lib/artifacts/artifact-content-channel.ts (the channel itself: the class resolution, the per-class caps and the named-absence contract), the module it reaches for a projection digest, and src/lib/artifacts/local-disk-blob-store.ts (the canonical server-side byte read the text arm streams the pinned revision through — the same read the artifact page's own markdown handler uses). Nothing leaves.

NARROWING WAS TRIED AND MEASURED, not assumed. Both runtime edges were moved behind dynamic import() inside the async builder and the gate measured the same +3 on all four routes, so the scanner follows them and laziness buys nothing. Folding the modules in is not available either: the channel is the ONE definition every display reads a projection from, and re-deriving a class, a cap or an absence here is exactly the duplication the enabler exists to prevent; the blob store is the host's one byte road. The digest fallback that would have added a fourth edge was dropped instead — a configuration with no recorded digest now answers an absence rather than being sealed to a value the gate never recorded.

MEASURED BY THE GATE ITSELF on the merged tree, with the companion extension fleet cloned pinned: /api/a2a 1767 (ceiling 1764, +3), /api/llm-bridge 1777 (ceiling 1774, +3), /api/mcp 1759 (ceiling 1756, +3), /chat 1862 (ceiling 1859, +3); /sign-in unchanged and left exactly where main committed it, record included. Restoring only this one file to the merge commit's version measures clean on every tracked route, which is the per-file attribution. The carried-forward records these raises replace are RETIRED BY THE RAISE, which is the one lifecycle the gate allows for an annotation whose ceiling moves; nothing they absorbed is re-absorbed here.
